text:
nina: Heads-up: PR #4722 touches the /files.upload API ref. The top example shows JSON with \"content\" (base64) but the SDK snippets and curl examples use multipart/form-data with a 'file' field. The OpenAPI requestBody is currently set to application/json. This is inconsistent and will confuse users. cc @alex @sam

alex: Yikes. Which files contain the conflicting snippets?

nina: docs/apis/files.md (top example was changed in the PR to JSON), sdk_snippets/files/upload_examples.md still uses multipart, and the JS example in apis/examples.md uses fetch with formdata.

sam: Runtime accepts both shapes today (we do coercion to support both) but legacy clients rely on multipart. We need to pick canonical shape in the API ref (prefer multipart for actual file uploads) and update OpenAPI examples to show multipart/form-data example plus a JSON alternative note.

alex: Agreed. Multipart is more practical for large files. Proposed plan:
- Set OpenAPI requestBody media type to multipart/form-data with schema showing 'file' (binary) and optional 'metadata' JSON string.
- Keep a secondary JSON example showing base64 content under an \"alternate examples\" section and explicitly mark it as discouraged/legacy.
- Update SDK snippets (JS/Python/Go) to use streaming/multipart examples.
- Add migration note in CHANGELOG.md and an example curl multipart command.

docs-bot: Added checklist to PR: update OpenAPI media type -> multipart/form-data, sync SDK snippets, add migration note, run docs build.

nina: Can someone supply a canonical curl snippet we can use? I can patch the OpenAPI examples and top-of-page copy once we decide.

sdk-bot: Suggested curl multipart example (for inclusion):

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/files.upload" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -F "file=@/path/to/report.pdf" \
  -F "metadata={\"description\":\"monthly report\"};type=application/json"
```

alex: That looks good. For the Python SDK snippet prefer streaming to avoid loading into memory: use open('report.pdf','rb') and client.files.upload(file=fp, metadata={...}). I'll draft the snippet.

sam: Also update the JS example to use a fetch + FormData snippet and a Node example using form-data or fetch with FormData. Add a short note: \"If you must send base64 in JSON, include contentSize and set contentEncoding: base64; this path is deprecated and will be removed in next minor.\"

nina: Let's also add a migration one-liner for teams who bulk-converted JSON base64 fields during earlier migrations: a jq/perl command that decodes base64 and writes files locally, or a sed to convert shape? Maybe too heavy. Suggest adding a small Python script in the migration note that iterates records and re-uploads via multipart.

docs-bot: Reminder set: add deprecation banner to /files.upload API ref page and link to migration example. Marking PR as needs-docs-review after patch.

alex: I'll prepare the SDK snippet patches and the Node/Browser examples. Nina, can you update the OpenAPI examples and top-level copy?

nina: Yes, I'll update docs/apis/files.md and the OpenAPI example block. Will also include the curl multipart snippet and the discouraged JSON example with explicit warning.

sam: Once patches are up I'll run local docs build and smoke test the examples. Also propose adding an integration test that validates the example curl actually succeeds against the staging mock.

docs-bot: Checklists: update OpenAPI, update SDK snippets (js/python/go), add migration blurb in CHANGELOG, add integration smoke test, run docs build.

alex: Pushing SDK changes now. Will request @nina review when done.

nina: Thanks. Please ping when both PRs are ready; I'll queue for merge after docs CI passes. :thumbsup:
